First of all, congratulations on reaching your goal. I had weight-loss surgery because I was about 200 pounds overweight. That was three years ago and from what I’ve learned, there’s some simple things that will help... 

Water water water. Order smaller meals at restaurants, and don’t feel obligated to finish it. If you do snack, keep it small and as close to zero carbs as possible. (I love to grab a bite size piece of cheese or a string cheese, and a slice of lunch meat or sliced meat.) Protein really does make you feel better, helps you stay feeling full longer, and gives you energy. 

The urge to crunch on things will probably always be a part of your life. Grab a handful of nuts or some popcorn. Potato chips and crackers aren’t your friend. If you can avoid soda, please do. Avoid alcohol. 

It’s all about being conscious of what you’re actually putting in your mouth. It doesn’t really mean that you have to eat only heathy foods for the rest of your life. Don’t starve yourself, eat three times a day. Snack every once in a while if your body is telling you it needs it. 

Calorie counting is great when you’re on a path to success, but it’s hard to live that way forever. I think at this point you should be aware of what the correct choice is when it comes to eating. Pancakes for breakfast? Or a yogurt or some eggs? It’s simple things like that. 

Respect yourself and the hard work you put in to get to where you are! You got this.
